job.title: Analyst, Workforce and Governance Advisory
job.description:
About Orchard Advisory

Orchard Talent Group is one of Australia's leading social purpose executive search firms. We are reimagining talent for impact.

Aged care, disability, mental health, healthcare and community services are changing fast. Funding reform, tighter regulation, workforce shortages and rising scrutiny of leadership and pay are reshaping how these organisations are structured and governed. Roles designed for one funding model are still carrying functions the next one cannot pay for. Boards and executives have to decide what their roles can now contain, at what ratio, and at what cost to care. Orchard Advisory exists to answer those questions with evidence.
We advise on workforce modelling, organisation and role design, remuneration and governance. Our search and solutions practices place several thousand people a year across the care economy, from frontline coordinators to chief executives. That gives our advice a current view of what roles cost, how they behave in the labour market, and whether a role as designed can actually be filled. Most of our clients are in the care economy. We also work with government and public purpose organisations, and with investor-backed providers.

The role

This is the first dedicated appointment into the advisory practice. You will work alongside an experienced partner across whole engagements, from scoping through to the board presentation. The partner leading this practice has held chief executive roles running organisational reform, and has led workforce and operating model design inside a major advisory firm, so this is work you will learn from someone who has both recommended these decisions and been accountable for making them.
Your work will turn workforce, financial and regulatory data into advice boards can act on. You will build the models, do the field work, draft the reports, and present findings alongside the partner.

The work you will deliver
  • Workforce modelling and cost optimisation: costing what roles actually do, reallocating functions across adjacent roles, setting sustainable ratios, and testing them against a range of price, funding and utilisation assumptions
  • Organisation and role design: designing roles and structures that the funding model can sustain, the handoffs between them, and the success profiles that follow
  • Remuneration reviews: benchmarking executive and director remuneration so boards can set pay that is fair, affordable and defensible
  • Board capability and effectiveness reviews: skills matrices, board dynamics and governance frameworks, so boards know whether they have what the organisation needs next
What you will do
  • Build and maintain the quantitative models behind workforce costing, ratio analysis, labour cost modelling and remuneration benchmarking, documented so a client can re-run them after we hand over
  • Get out into the field, because how a service model is executed is rarely what the documentation says
  • Write board-ready reports and presentations that make complex findings simple to act on
  • Take part in client workshops, stakeholder interviews and board presentations alongside the partner
  • Grow Orchard's benchmarking datasets and methodologies from every engagement, so each piece of work makes the next one faster
  • Use AI tools and environments, Claude and Claude Code in particular, to automate research and accelerate analysis
What you will bring
  • Two to five years in management consulting (Big Four human capital or workforce advisory, a remuneration or governance boutique, public policy, or organisational psychology), or related experience and the curiosity to apply it here
  • Strong quantitative skills, and the judgement to turn data into a commercial narrative. Comfort building a cost or ratio model from the ground up, and publishing your assumptions so others can test them
  • Clear, confident writing, and the presence to hold a conversation with a chief executive or a director
  • Willingness to spend time in the field, including interstate travel where an engagement calls for it, and the manner to be welcome wherever care is delivered
  • Genuine interest in Australian industrial relations, workforce compliance and corporate governance
  • Comfort in a practice still being built, where you move between deep analysis and open team discussion
Who we are looking for

You are curious and meticulous, and you enjoy problems that have no playbook yet. You are as happy inside a cost model as you are reading governance literature or working out how an AI workflow could take a week out of a project.
You are analytical and pragmatic. You know data matters only when it helps someone make a better decision. What motivates you is seeing your work change how an organisation is led, in a sector where that shows up in the care people receive.
Our values are passionate, accountable, collaborative and empathetic. We look for people who recognise themselves in those words.

What success looks like

We measure this role on three things:
  • The clarity, accuracy and usefulness of the advice our clients receive
  • The growth of Orchard's benchmarking datasets and methodologies
  • The workflows you design that let the practice take on more work without losing quality
Why this role

You will be the second person in a practice with a clear market and an established firm behind it. You will see whole engagements, not slices of them. You will be in the room with boards and chief executives from your first month. And you will help decide what this practice becomes.

How to apply

Apply online at orchardtalent.com.au by submitting your CV and a cover letter. Your cover letter should outline how you’d contribute to a new practice and what skills and talents you bring. For further information or a confidential discussion, contact Adam Dent, Partner, Advisory at advisory@orchardtalent.com.au

job.title: Chief Operating Officer
job.description:
The organisation
Just Better Care is an established Australian provider of in-home aged care and disability support, operating through a national network of locally owned franchises. Supporting approximately 8,500 people across Australia, the organisation combines the strength of a recognised national brand with local relationships and personalised care. In 2026, Just Better Care was ranked Australia’s #1 Best Workplace™ in Healthcare & Social Assistance (Large Organisation category) by Great Place To Work®, reflecting the culture and commitment of its people. Just Better Care was also named among Australia’s Top 10 Franchises for 2026 by 10 THOUSAND FEET Research, based on franchise owner satisfaction survey results.
 
The opportunity
This newly created executive appointment offers the opportunity to influence Just Better Care’s future direction at a pivotal point for the home care and disability sectors. Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the COO will strengthen the commercial performance, engagement and capability of the national franchise network, while supporting disciplined, sustainable growth. The role provides executive oversight of franchise development, strategic supplier partnerships and the company-owned office, which serves as a model for new initiatives across the network.
The Chief Operating Officer will:
  • Build trusted relationships with franchise partners, including key strategic franchise businesses, strengthening engagement, commercial capability and accountability for performance.
  • Translate strategy into measurable network priorities, using business planning, financial insights and operational data to improve growth, productivity and customer outcomes.
  • Oversee franchise development, strategic procurement partnerships and the company-owned office, working with the Transformation team to pilot and implement practical improvements across the network.
  • Lead and develop a lean, high-performing operational team, collaborating closely with Clinical Governance & Assurance, People & Culture and other specialist teams to align commercial objectives with quality, compliance and customer outcomes.
About you
You are a commercially astute, energetic and highly engaging leader who can build credibility with independent business owners and inspire action across a geographically dispersed network. You bring senior operational leadership experience from home care, aged care, disability services, healthcare or a franchised service environment, with a strong understanding of the Australian aged care and NDIS landscape. Experience in franchise development, procurement or strategic partnerships will be valuable.
Equally important is your ability to move between strategy and execution. You thrive in a lean executive team, bring sound financial judgement and know how to coach, influence and challenge stakeholders with empathy and confidence. You understand the importance of partnering with specialist quality and governance teams, rather than treating compliance as separate from commercial decision-making. A willingness to travel interstate and engage directly with franchise partners is essential.
 
What’s on offer
A newly created, senior executive role with direct access to the CEO and genuine influence over the organisation’s future.
  • The opportunity to shape growth across aged care, disability and private services through an established national brand.
  • A highly visible, relationship-led mandate with scope to strengthen franchise partnerships and develop the network.
  • A collaborative, agile leadership environment, working alongside specialist clinical, assurance, people and transformation teams.
  • A Manly-based role with interstate travel and a compelling opportunity to make an impact nationally.

job.description:
The organisation
Vision Australia is a leading national organisation with a proud 150-year legacy. We're passionately pursuing our mission to empower people who are blind or have low vision to live the life they choose. Our dedicated team of around 850 employees and more than 2,000 volunteers delivers vital services across education, employment, independence and social inclusion, from specialist allied health and employment support to assistive technology and Seeing Eye Dogs.

The opportunity
Vision Australia is seeking an accomplished and values-led Chief Client Officer (CCO) to lead the transformation and integration of its national client services portfolio. Reporting to the CEO and working closely with the Board and its Committees, the CCO will play a critical role in delivering high-quality, person-centred services while strengthening operational performance, clinical governance and financial sustainability.

As a key member of the Executive Team, you will lead a diverse portfolio encompassing Client Services, National Programs, Employment Services and Vision Store, supporting more than 17,000 clients annually. Working in partnership with the Chief Governance Risk and Compliance Officer, you will embed consistent service models, strengthen clinical quality and safeguarding, and drive greater coordination across teams, regions and funding streams.

This is a significant opportunity to shape the future of service delivery at Vision Australia. You will build high-performing teams and optimise services to improve access, client outcomes and long-term sustainability, ensuring the organisation continues to deliver meaningful impact for people who are blind or have low vision.

About you
You are an accomplished executive leader with extensive experience overseeing complex, geographically dispersed service operations, ideally within health, disability, aged care or broader human services environments. You bring a strong track record of leading service transformation, integrating multidisciplinary teams and driving operational excellence, with the credibility to influence at Executive and Board level.

You combine strong clinical governance capability with commercial acumen and a deep commitment to person-centred care. You have demonstrated success improving service quality, safeguarding and client outcomes while strengthening financial performance and organisational sustainability. A relevant clinical qualification, together with current AHPRA registration or membership of an appropriate professional body for a self-regulating allied health profession, will be highly regarded. Applications from exceptional executives with substantial clinical governance experience are also encouraged.

You are a collaborative, pragmatic and values-led leader who can navigate complexity, build organisational capability and inspire teams through change. Lived experience of blindness or low vision will be highly valued, and we actively encourage applications from candidates who share Vision Australia's commitment to inclusion and meaningful social impact.

What’s on offer
A competitive remuneration package will be offered, commensurate with skills and experience.

The role may be based in Brisbane, Sydney or Melbourne, with Vision Australia offering a high degree of flexibility. Interstate travel will be required for Board, Committee and organisational commitments.

Nepean Blue Mountains Local Health District (NBMLHD) is part of NSW Health and cares for communities across Penrith, the Blue Mountains, the Hawkesbury and Lithgow. job.title: Staff Specialist O&G, Northern NSW Local Health District, Lismore
job.description:
The organisation
Northern NSW Local Health District (NNSWLHD) cares for over 300,000 people across the Northern Rivers, a sub-tropical region of rainforest, coastline and breathtaking natural attractions stretching from Tweed Heads to Grafton. Lismore, the region’s cultural and economic capital, sits between the Gondwana rainforest and the Pacific Ocean, just 200 km south of Brisbane.

Across 12 hospitals and 21 community health centres, NNSWLHD clinicians have a direct impact on the health and wellbeing of regional communities, while staying connected to best-practice care across Australia through training networks and partnerships with local and metropolitan tertiary education providers.  Major capital projects underway across several facilities reflect the district’s investment in the future of care in Northern NSW.
 
The opportunity
This is a unique opportunity to join a close-knit and supportive Obstetrics and Gynaecology team at Lismore Base Hospital, providing specialist care to women and families across Northern NSW. The department is a busy, well-established unit managing approximately 1,300 births each year, with obstetric care provided for babies from 32 weeks’ gestation.

Lismore Base Hospital is appointing additional Staff Specialists to strengthen its workforce and support the long-term sustainability of the service, and has maintained a positive, cohesive culture and a strong commitment to high-quality patient care.
 
Reporting to the Head of Department, you will:
  • Deliver safe, contemporary and evidence-based obstetric and gynaecological care
  • Supervise, teach and mentor junior medical officers, registrars and other healthcare professionals
  • Contribute to clinical governance, quality improvement and service development
  • Participate in the on-call roster and help build a sustainable specialist service
 
About you
You are a Specialist Obstetrician and Gynaecologist eligible for registration with the Medical Board of Australia, including through specialist international medical graduate pathways. You bring recent clinical experience across obstetrics, antenatal care, general gynaecology and surgery, and you enjoy the breadth and variety of generalist practice.

You are a collaborative, adaptable and patient-centred clinician who thrives in a close-knit team. You value collegiality, shared decision-making and a consistent approach to clinical practice. Your communication and counselling skills allow you to balance clinical recommendations with informed patient preferences, supporting women to make decisions about their care.

You are committed to teaching, continuing education and quality improvement, and are available to participate in the on-call roster and respond on site within a reasonable time. You are willing and able to provide the full scope of services offered by the department, including termination-of-pregnancy care, which is an essential component of the position. A valid NSW Working With Children Check is required.
 
Why join Lismore Base Hospital?
This is an opportunity to build a rewarding career while making a meaningful contribution to women’s health across Northern NSW.
  • Appointment under the Staff Specialists (State) Award,
  • Full-time and fractional appointments, with flexibility for individual and family circumstances,
  • Broad generalist practice, with support to develop particular clinical interests,
  • The opportunity to contribute to Aboriginal women’s health, including through the Aboriginal Medical Service in Casino.
  • A relaxed, sub-tropical lifestyle with rainforest and ocean close to home.
  • Introduction to a culturally rich city which proudly displays its artistic heritage.
 
How to apply

job.title: Executive Director, Policy - The Cabinet Office NSW
job.description:
• Lead policy, strategy and integrity from the heart of government
  • Provide trusted, impartial advice to the Premier and Cabinet
  • Shape policy on complex issues to improve the lives of the people of NSW
This is an opportunity to lead a policy branch at the centre of NSW Government, providing evidence-based advice on some of the most significant policy issues facing NSW.

About us
The Cabinet Office operates at the heart of NSW Government, supporting the Premier and Cabinet with expert policy advice informed by data, evidence, and a focus on the bigger picture. The Cabinet Office coordinates and often leads policy reform to drive the Government’s priorities, and advances NSW’s interests at the national level through strategic advice on intergovernmental matters. The Cabinet Office is the steward of the NSW Cabinet system, promoting adherence to Cabinet conventions and good Cabinet practice to support good government decision-making.

The Cabinet Office is made up of four groups: the Office of General Counsel; Social Policy and Intergovernmental Relations; Energy, Environment and Evidence; and Economic, Housing and Infrastructure Policy. Its people are guided by the values of integrity, trust, service and accountability, including a commitment to apolitical and non-partisan advice.
 
The role
As Executive Director, Policy, you will lead at the policy branch level, setting the direction of research, analysis and policy development across key portfolio areas. You will provide timely, expert and authoritative advice to the Deputy Secretary, the Secretary, the Premier and Cabinet, and manage the Cabinet process for your portfolio areas. Working closely with the Premier, Ministers and senior executives across government, you will shape policy, legislation, programs and machinery of government arrangements that drive the Government's priorities.

You will identify the interdependencies and trade-offs between new policy and Budget proposals across portfolios, giving decision-makers a clear, whole-of-government view. When urgent issues arise, you will adjust your branch's focus quickly while continuing to deliver the Government's long-term policy agenda.
